abiathar.title: Abiathar
abiathar.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
abiathar.note: He was the only priest to get out of Nob alive when Saul had the place killed, and he went straight to David and stayed his priest through the running years and the reign. At the end he backed Adonijah instead of Solomon, and Solomon sent him away from the priesthood rather than kill him.

abigal.title: Abigal
abigal.about: David's wife living at the time of United Monarchy
abigal.note: A variant spelling of Abigail, David's wife. She rode out to stop David wiping out her first husband Nabal's household, and it worked. Once Nabal was dead she married David.

abishai.title: Abishai
abishai.about: David's warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
abishai.note: David's nephew, and the most willing man he had. He is credited with three hundred killed on his own. Twice he offered to finish one of David's enemies on the spot, Saul asleep in the camp and Shimei cursing on the road, and both times David told him no.

abner.title: Abner
abner.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
abner.note: Saul's cousin, and the commander of his army. When Saul died he did not stop: he kept the war going between David and what was left of Saul's house.

achish.title: Achish
achish.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
achish.note: He is the Philistine king of Gath, and he took David in while David was running from Saul.

adullam.title: Adullam
adullam.note: A Canaanite royal city in the Shephelah, near the valley of Elah. David killed Goliath in that valley. Later, running from Saul, he hid in a cave near Adullam, and his family joined him there, and so did everyone in distress.

ahimelech.title: Ahimelech
ahimelech.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
ahimelech.note: The priest at Nob. He helped David, who was fleeing Saul, without knowing it, and gave him the consecrated bread and Goliath's sword. Once Doeg reported it, Saul had him and the rest of the priests at Nob massacred.

ahimelech-3.title: Ahimelech
ahimelech-3.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
ahimelech-3.note: One of 3 men called Ahimelech. This one is a warrior from the united kingdom, named once in 1 Samuel.

ahinoam.title: Ahinoam
ahinoam.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
ahinoam.note: The Ahinoam from Jezreel whom David married, mother of his firstborn son Amnon, and a different woman from Saul's wife of the same name.

ahitub.title: Ahitub
ahitub.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
ahitub.note: Ahimelech's father, in Israel's high priestly line.

amalek.title: Amalek
amalek.note: Esau's grandson. The Amalekites who came from him attacked the weak rear of Israel's column in the wilderness, and God declared war on Amalek for it. Saul's half-done obedience against them later cost him the kingdom.

aroer-3.title: Aroer
aroer-3.note: 1 Samuel names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

athach.title: Athach
athach.note: David sent it a share of the spoil he took back from the Amalekite raiders who hit Ziklag, a gift to the elders of Judah who had put up with him in his outlaw years. The name occurs nowhere else, and some suggest a copyist's slip for Ether.

besor.title: Besor
besor.note: A brook in southern Judah. Two hundred of David's men were too worn out to cross it and stayed behind while the rest chased the Amalekite raiders. David then insisted that the men who stayed with the supplies share the spoil equally.

beth-el-2.title: Beth-el
beth-el-2.note: Named once, in 1 Samuel, and nowhere else.

caleb.title: Caleb
caleb.about: Joshua's compatriot living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest
caleb.note: One of the twelve spies Moses sent into Canaan. He and Joshua were the only two who came back telling Israel to trust God and take the land, and the rest of that generation paid for ignoring them with forty years in the wilderness.

carmel.title: Carmel
carmel.note: Elijah's contest with the prophets of Baal happened on this mountain ridge on Israel's Mediterranean coast. Fire came down from heaven when Elijah prayed, and Baal had nothing to answer with.

carmelite.title: Carmelite
carmelite.note: Here it means someone from Carmel in Judah's hill country, not Mount Carmel in the north. Nabal was a Carmelite, the rich fool who insulted David, and so was his wife Abigail, who married David after Nabal died.

cherethims-2.title: Cherethims
cherethims-2.note: The people themselves, close neighbours of the Philistines and likely from Crete. Ezekiel and Zephaniah both name them in oracles of judgment.

chorashan.title: Chorashan
chorashan.note: After he rescued the Ziklag captives from the Amalekites, David sent gifts from the plunder to a string of towns, and this was one. It is generally identified with Ashan, a town of Simeon in the Negev of Judah.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling a kingdom bigger than any native king held before or after. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

doeg.title: Doeg
doeg.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
doeg.note: Saul's chief herdsman, an Edomite, who told Saul that the priest Ahimelech had helped David. Saul's own men would not kill the priests of Nob. Doeg did it himself, eighty-five priests and the whole town with them.

edomite.title: Edomite
edomite.note: Esau's descendants, living in Seir south and east of the Dead Sea. Kin to Israel and at odds with it for most of the record. Egyptian texts mention Edom as early as the thirteenth century BC, and its capital Busayra and the copper works at Khirbat en Nahas have both been excavated.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

elah.title: Elah
elah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elah.note: David killed Goliath in the Valley of Elah, the terebinth valley in Judah's lowlands, with the two armies on opposite slopes. The name also belongs to Elah son of Baasha, king of Israel, murdered while drunk by Zimri, his own chariot commander. Khirbet Qeiyafa above the valley has a tenth century BC fort and one of the earliest Hebrew inscriptions.

en-dor.title: En-dor
en-dor.note: Home of the medium Saul went to in disguise the night before his last battle. It lay in Issachar's land, near where Deborah and Barak beat Sisera. Endur, southeast of Mount Tabor, keeps the name.

en-gedi.title: En-gedi
en-gedi.note: An oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea, fed by a spring that drops some 600 feet down the cliffs. David hid in its caves from Saul and spared Saul's life there. A Chalcolithic temple on the site is far older than Israel in Canaan.

eshtemoa.title: Eshtemoa
eshtemoa.note: David sent some of the Amalekite plunder to the elders of Eshtemoa, a priestly town south of Hebron, for standing by him in his outlaw years. It survives as es-Samu, where old ruins have been found.

gad-2.title: Gad
gad-2.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
gad-2.note: A prophet of the united monarchy, and nothing to do with Jacob's son. He first turns up in 1 Samuel 22:5, comes back in 2 Samuel 24, and Chronicles names him again.

gallim.title: Gallim
gallim.note: Michal was given to Palti of Gallim after Saul took her away from David. Isaiah lists the town, in Benjamin north of Jerusalem, among the places panicking as the Assyrian army comes on.

gath.title: Gath
gath.note: Goliath's hometown, one of the five Philistine cities. The captured ark brought disaster on it, David later hid there with King Achish while running from Saul, and in the end David took it. Most identify it with Tell es-Safi, where a potsherd turned up carrying two names related to Goliath.

geshuri.title: Geshuri
geshuri.note: David married Maacah, daughter of Talmai, the king of Geshur, and so these people were Absalom's family on his mother's side. Their small Aramean kingdom lay east of the Sea of Galilee.

gezrites.title: Gezrites
gezrites.note: David raided them from Ziklag along with the Geshurites and Amalekites. Most read the name as Girzites, an otherwise unknown desert tribe in the Negev toward Egypt, and not the people of Gezer.

gilboa.title: Gilboa
gilboa.note: Saul died on these hills above the Jezreel Valley. The Philistines broke his army, three of his sons fell, Jonathan among them, and Saul, badly wounded, took his own life. David's lament curses Gilboa never to have dew or rain.

goliath.title: Goliath
goliath.about: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
goliath.note: The Philistine champion from Gath whom the young David killed in the valley of Elah. The traditional Hebrew text makes him over nine feet, while the Dead Sea Scrolls and the earliest Greek give about six foot nine. One later passage credits Elhanan, and Chronicles makes Elhanan's man Goliath's brother.

hachilah.title: Hachilah
hachilah.note: David hid from Saul on this hill in the wilderness. From here he and Abishai crept into Saul's camp at night and took his spear and water jug instead of killing him.

hebron.title: Hebron
hebron.note: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.

hereth.title: Hereth
hereth.note: A forest in Judah. David hid there with his growing band after leaving his parents with the king of Moab, and the prophet Gad told him to go. Where it was is unknown.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

hormah.title: Hormah
hormah.note: Its name means "devoted to destruction", and it was first called Zephath. Israel was beaten there after going into Canaan without the Lord, following the spies' report. Later Israel vowed to destroy the cities of the region, and the vow, kept under Joshua, gave the town its name.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jattir.title: Jattir
jattir.note: A priests' town in the hill country of Judah, given to Aaron's line. David sent its elders a share of the Amalekite plunder, as he did for many towns while he was on the run. It is identified with Khirbet Attir, south of Hebron.

jerahmeelites.title: Jerahmeelites
jerahmeelites.note: A clan of Judah, Jerahmeel's people, living in the Negev. While David was based at Ziklag under Philistine protection he raided their country, and later he sent them a share of the Amalekite plunder as allies.

jesse.title: Jesse
jesse.about: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
jesse.note: Obed's son and Boaz and Ruth's grandson, a man of some standing in Bethlehem with eight sons, the youngest David. Isaiah's "stem of Jesse" is David's family, and the "root of Jesse" is the Messiah. The last we see of him, David is getting him a safe place with the king of Moab.

jezreel-2.title: Jezreel
jezreel-2.note: Not the northern valley. This Jezreel is a town in the hill country near Hebron, listed in Joshua 15:56.

joab.title: Joab
joab.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
joab.note: David's nephew, and the commander of his army for most of the reign. He was loyal to what David needed rather than what David said: he arranged Uriah's death when asked, killed Absalom when told not to, and murdered Abner and Amasa under cover of friendship. David never forgave Absalom. On David's word Solomon had Joab killed, even holding on to the altar.

jonathan.title: Jonathan
jonathan.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
jonathan.note: Saul's eldest son, heir to the throne, and David's friend. He made a covenant with David knowing it cost him the crown. Once, with only his armour-bearer, he climbed a cliff and started a rout of the Philistine army. He died with Saul and two brothers on Mount Gilboa, and David's lament for him says his love was "surpassing the love of women."

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

keilah.title: Keilah
keilah.note: David saved this walled town from a Philistine raid while Saul was hunting him. Then he learned they would have handed him over if Saul came, and he moved on into the wilderness of Ziph.

kenite.title: Kenite
kenite.note: They were a wandering clan close to Midian, outside the twelve tribes but mostly friendly to Israel. Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, was a Kenite priest, and Jael, Heber the Kenite's wife, killed Sisera.

laish-2.title: Laish
laish-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
laish-2.note: 1 Samuel and 2 Samuel name him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

maoch.title: Maoch
maoch.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
maoch.note: Father of Achish, the Philistine king of Gath who took David in when Saul was hunting him. A later king of Gath, Achish son of Maacah, turns up in Solomon's time, and whether Maoch and Maacah are the same man or the name just ran in that royal house is uncertain.

maon.title: Maon
maon.note: About seven miles south of Hebron, in the Judean hill country. David hid from Saul in the wilderness named after it, and Nabal, whose widow Abigail married David, kept his flocks there. The ruins, now Tell Ma'in, still mark the spot.

michal.title: Michal
michal.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
michal.note: Saul's younger daughter. David won her by killing two hundred Philistines, and she saved his life by letting him down through a window when Saul's men came. Saul then gave her to another man; David took her back as king, but she despised him for dancing before the ark, and she had no children to the end of her life.

mizpeh.title: Mizpeh
mizpeh.note: Another spelling of Mizpah, the watchpost name given to several places in Israel.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

nabal.title: Nabal
nabal.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
nabal.note: A rich, hard man. David's men had guarded his shepherds, and when David asked for food Nabal sent back insults. Only his wife Abigail, riding out with a generous gift, kept David from killing his whole household. When she told Nabal ten days later what he had nearly brought on them, he seems to have had a stroke, and he died. David married Abigail.

ner.title: Ner
ner.about: Saul's uncle living at the time of United Monarchy
ner.note: Father of Abner, Saul's army commander. Ner was Saul's grandfather or great-uncle, depending on how the genealogies are fitted together.

nob.title: Nob
nob.note: A town of priests near Jerusalem. David came here running from Saul, and the priest Ahimelech gave him the consecrated bread and Goliath's sword. Saul had the priests of Nob killed for it.

palti.title: Palti
palti.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
palti.note: 1 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

paran.title: Paran
paran.note: Ishmael grew up in this wilderness after Hagar was sent away with him, and Israel camped there for part of the long march.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

rachal.title: Rachal
rachal.note: David sent a share of the plunder from his Amalekite raid to the elders here, a town in Judah's Negev. Nobody has located it.

ramah.title: Ramah
ramah.note: Samuel's hometown, and where he was buried. The name was common enough that several towns carried it. Jeremiah's Rachel weeping for her children is set here too.

samuel.title: Samuel
samuel.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
samuel.note: Hannah prayed for a son and gave him to the Lord before he was born. He grew up to be the last of the judges and the first great prophet. Israel's first two kings were both anointed by him.

saul.title: Saul
saul.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
saul.note: Israel's first king, found while he was out looking for his father's lost donkeys and anointed by Samuel in private before the tribes confirmed him.

sela-hammalekoth.title: Sela-hammalekoth
sela-hammalekoth.note: Saul and David were on opposite sides of this mountain in the wilderness of Maon, and Saul was closing in. Then a messenger came with word of the Philistines, and Saul turned back. The name means rock of escape.

shunem.title: Shunem
shunem.note: A village of Issachar near Jezreel. The Philistines camped here before the battle on Mount Gilboa where Saul and his sons died, and a woman here built a room for Elisha.

siphmoth.title: Siphmoth
siphmoth.note: After David took back the plunder from an Amalekite raid, he sent a share to the elders of Judah in the Negev towns where he had been sheltered as a fugitive. Siphmoth was one of those towns.

urim.title: Urim
urim.note: The Urim and Thummim sat in the high priest's breastpiece. They were used to put yes-or-no questions to God. How they actually worked, nobody knows.

zeruiah.title: Zeruiah
zeruiah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
zeruiah.note: David's sister, the mother of Joab, Abishai and Asahel. David said the sons of Zeruiah were too much for him.

ziklag.title: Ziklag
ziklag.note: Achish of Gath gave this town in the Negev to David while he was running from Saul, and David lived there more than a year. Amalekites burned it while he was away and took the women and children, and he went after them and got everyone back.

ziph.title: Ziph
ziph.note: David hid in the wilderness around Ziph, southeast of Hebron, while Saul was hunting him. The people of Ziph told Saul where he was, twice.

ziphim.title: Ziphim
ziphim.note: The people of Ziph, who twice gave David's hiding place away to Saul. Psalm 54 is headed with that betrayal.
